beats.intro: Chapter three, lesson two. Cohesion, and keeping temperature steady. [[tree]]A tall tree lifts water higher than most pumps could. [[lake]]And a lake stays mild while the air swings hot and cold. [[both]]Both come from one thing: hydrogen bonds between water molecules.
beats.cohes: Zoom into a drop of water. [[pull]]Each molecule has a slightly negative oxygen end, and slightly positive hydrogen ends. [[bond]]So a hydrogen on one molecule is drawn toward the oxygen of its neighbor. [[many]]One bond is weak. It breaks and re-forms in a fraction of a second. [[team]]But each molecule has several neighbors, so together the bonds hold the liquid as one body. [[name]]Water molecules sticking to each other like this is called cohesion.
beats.tree: Now back to the tree. [[push]]Inside the trunk are narrow tubes, and a column of water fills each one from the roots to the leaves. [[leaf]]At the leaves, water evaporates into the air. [[pull]]Each molecule that leaves tugs on the one below it, and because of cohesion, the whole chain follows, like a rope being drawn up. [[wall]]The tube walls help too. Water also sticks to other materials, here the wall, through hydrogen bonds. That is adhesion, and it keeps the column from sliding back down. [[gravity]]So gravity pulls down, but evaporation pulls up, cohesion links the chain, and adhesion grips the wall.
beats.surf: Cohesion also shows at the top of a pond. [[under]]A molecule deep in the water is pulled equally in every direction. [[top]]One at the surface has water beside it and below it, but none above. [[skin]]So it is pulled inward and sideways, and the surface acts like a stretched skin. [[strider]]That resistance to being broken is surface tension, and it lets a water strider stand on the pond.
beats.q1: Quick check. What would go wrong in the trunk?
beats.temp: Part two is heat. [[fast]]In warm water, the molecules dart around quickly. [[slow]]In cold water, they drift slowly. [[ke]]Moving things have kinetic energy, and the random motion of molecules is thermal energy. [[avg]]Temperature is the average kinetic energy of a molecule in the sample. It is not the total. [[total]]A bathtub of warm water holds far more thermal energy than a cup of boiling water, though the cup has the higher temperature. [[heat]]Heat is thermal energy on the move, passing from the warmer body to the cooler one.
beats.units: How do we count heat? [[cal]]One calorie is the heat that raises one gram of water by one degree Celsius. [[kcal]]A kilocalorie is a thousand calories, and it is what food labels call a Calorie. [[joule]]The joule is the standard unit of energy, and one calorie equals four point one eight four joules. [[mult]]So one kilocalorie is four thousand, one hundred eighty-four joules.
beats.spec: Water takes a lot of heat to change its temperature. [[water]]One calorie warms one gram of water by one degree. That number, heat per gram per degree, is the specific heat, and for water it is one. [[hotsame]]Now give six hundred calories to a hundred and fifty grams of water, and the same to dry sand. [[calc]]Six hundred divided by a hundred and fifty is four degrees. [[sand]]Sand has a specific heat of about a fifth of that, so the same heat warms it by about twenty degrees. [[high]]Water has a high specific heat.
beats.why: Why is water so stubborn? [[in]]When heat flows in, a large share goes into breaking hydrogen bonds. [[brk]]Energy spent snapping bonds is energy that does not speed the molecules up, so the temperature climbs slowly. [[out]]When water cools, bonds form again, and they release that energy as heat. [[buf]]So water soaks up heat slowly and gives it back slowly, and its temperature swings less.
beats.climate: That steadies whole places. [[day]]On a summer day the sun heats the sand fast, but the sea beside it warms only a little, taking heat from the air. [[night]]At night the sea gives heat back, and the air stays milder. [[coast]]This is why coasts have gentler weather than the middle of a continent. [[life]]And living cells, which are mostly water, are protected the same way.
beats.q2: Quick check. Find the temperature rise.
beats.evap: Last, evaporation. [[fast]]In liquid water, molecules move at many different speeds. [[leave]]The fastest ones at the surface can break all their bonds and escape as gas. [[left]]They carry away more than their share of kinetic energy, so the average of those left behind drops. The water cools. [[vap]]Turning one gram of water into vapor takes a lot of heat, about five hundred eighty calories at body temperature. This is the heat of vaporization. [[sweat]]Evaporating just one gram of sweat can cool a hundred grams of water by almost six degrees. [[pond]]That is why sweating cools you, and why evaporation steadies the temperature of ponds and leaves.
beats.wrap: To sum up. [[w1]]Hydrogen bonds give water cohesion, which helps lift it up trees and gives it surface tension. [[w2]]Temperature is average kinetic energy. Heat is thermal energy in transfer. [[w3]]Water's high specific heat, from bonds breaking and forming, steadies temperature. [[w4]]Evaporation cools, because the fastest molecules leave.
